summary: This component fetches and displays comments from Bluesky (a social media platform) on a blog post. It handles rendering the comment thread with proper text formatting for links, embeds like images and external links, and filters out blocked users while preserving replies to those users. The component also manages loading states and gracefully handles errors.

explanations.14: Bluesky uses byte positions in the text encoding, not JavaScript's character positions, so emoji and accented characters need special handling to slice correctly.
explanations.21: TextEncoder converts the post text into UTF-8 bytes so we can slice it using Bluesky's byte offsets instead of character positions.
explanations.28: We loop through each 'facet' (a marked-up section like a link) to reconstruct the text with proper React elements in place.
explanations.35: We search the facet's features array to find if this section is a link (identified by its $type property).
explanations.38: If the commenter is the site owner, we trust their links and render them as clickable anchors; otherwise we only show the link text to avoid spam.
explanations.73: We check if the 'external' property exists on the embed object instead of checking its $type, because the type system doesn't narrow based on $type alone here.
explanations.112: This interface extends the reply data with an additional 'depth' property to track how nested a comment is in the thread.
explanations.123: The double exclamation marks convert ownerHandle to a boolean and compare it with the comment author's handle to determine ownership.
explanations.124: We extract the post ID from the full URI by splitting on '/' and taking the last part.
explanations.127: We create a formatted date string using the browser's locale, showing the year, abbreviated month, day, and time.
explanations.138: We use inline padding that increases with each level of nesting, so replies are visually indented to show the conversation structure.
explanations.206: We extract the Bluesky record key from the front matter metadata of the current blog post.
explanations.216: We construct the Bluesky API URI that identifies this specific post, needed to fetch its replies from the public API.
explanations.223: We fetch both the comment thread and the moderation/blocked list in parallel using Promise.all to improve performance.
explanations.232: We create a single Set combining both inline-configured blocked handles and the handles from an external blocklist for efficient lookup.
explanations.237: This recursive function walks the nested reply tree, adding each reply to our flat array with its depth level, then recursively processes any replies to that comment.
explanations.243: We skip rendering blocked users but still recurse into their replies, so legitimate responses to spam comments remain visible.
explanations.270: We return null (render nothing) if there's no Bluesky record key configured or if an error occurred during fetch.
